PullRequest.Title: Engineering - bump @microsoft/copilot-sdk to 2.0.2-preview.2
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Bumps `@microsoft/copilot-sdk` from `2.0.1` to `2.0.2-preview.2`.

SDK 2.0.2-preview.2 streams Fusion output from the first model call instead of holding it back until the call finishes, which shortens time to first output for Fusion requests in the Agent Host. Multi-model drafts need separate client UX work, which is out of scope here.

### Changes

- Bump the SDK in `package.json` and `remote/package.json`. Only the nine SDK entries change in each lockfile.
- Bump `copilotRuntimeVersion` from `1.0.114` to `1.0.115-3` to match the runtime that the SDK bundles; the build checks that these agree.
- Adapt the Microsoft account flow to the SDK's renamed accounts API:
  - The Microsoft 365 Copilot account kind is now `microsoft365Copilot` instead of `loki`.
  - `accounts.get({ query: { kind: 'activeAccount' } })` is replaced by `accounts.getActive()`.
- Update the unit and provider-integration test fakes to the new API.
- Regenerate the managed-settings schema baseline: the bundled runtime adds the Windows sandbox `capabilities` allowlist and the macOS seatbelt `extraMachLookups` list.

### Notes

- `2.0.2-preview.2` is a prerelease. Newer previews exist; this pins the version that contains the Fusion streaming fixes.
- The version was not yet available from the package feed proxy at the time of writing, so a local `pnpm install` may need the public npm registry.

### Known blocker: extension consent retry

The bundled runtime now writes session permission decisions to the session log and restores them on resume. That includes the denial an extension keeps after a person declines its access to sensitive environment variables. The Agent Host's Retry after **Not Now** replaces the runtime and relied on a resume forgetting that denial, so with this SDK a retried canvas stays `failed` instead of asking again. These tests fail for that reason:

- `Copilot SDK - canvas lifecycle` › asks for sensitive environment consent without a tool call, keeps a denial until resume, and forgets session approvals on resume
- `Copilot extension environment consent` › asks before a canvas opened from the UI reads a sensitive variable, asks again after a retry, and keeps the approval across the refresh (default chat and peer chat)

This needs a decision on how Retry should clear the kept denial before the PR can merge.

### Validation

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed files: passed
- `scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAccountService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts`: passed (1175 passing)
- `scripts\test.bat --runGlob "vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/**/*.test.js"`: passed (15931 passing, 94 pending)
- `scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSdkManagedSettings.integrationTest.ts`: passed after regenerating the baseline with `AGENT_HOST_UPDATE_AHP_SNAPSHOTS=1` (11 passing)
- Checked that `copilotRuntimeVersion` matches `copilotCliVersion` in the installed SDK package: passed

- Linux (WSL), `AGENT_HOST_UPDATE_AHP_SNAPSHOTS=1 ./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotPromptsE2E.integrationTest.ts`: passed (24 passing); six baselines updated for the reworded `apply_patch` grammar
- Linux (WSL), `AGENT_HOST_REPLAY_RECORD=1 ./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --grep 'runtime compaction: a compacted conversation retains context after host restart'`: passed; then strict replay with `--grep 'runtime compaction'`: passed (3 passing)

Not run: the full Agent Host e2e suite locally, other provider-integration tests, and a manual Microsoft 365 sign-in.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold and warm Agent Host SDK/runtime startup, locally and remotely
Scenarios.CriticalPath: First SDK-dependent action awaits runtime asset resolution, client construction and client.start(); subsequent actions reuse the live client. Startup assets are resolved concurrently before the runtime starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the SDK symlink and check runtime, native module, SDK and extension bootstrap files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One realpath and five access calls per attempted package candidate; at most four candidates in the existing Linux fallback layout, not one lookup per session or model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same candidate selection and filesystem probes for SDK 2.0.1; only pinned package contents/version change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asset discovery must finish before cold client startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start the bundled Copilot runtime and establish its SDK connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One default runtime startup per successful cold acquisition, shared across callers; existing bounded configuration-change retries and separately scoped clients remain.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Already spawned the bundled runtime via the same SDK configuration and shared startup path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: First SDK-dependent action waits for startup; no additional spawn on warm default-client acquisition.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One shared default client per Agent Host lifecycle, plus existing separately scoped clients. Runtime lookup checks at most two package scopes and two Linux platform candidates; each candidate checks five assets.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: _ensureClientHealing and _clientStarting join concurrent default-client requests; _clientStopping is awaited before replacement. Five asset probes per package candidate use Promise.all; package candidates are tried serially. These controls are unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold startup resolves package paths and starts the runtime. Warm requests return _client without re-resolving or spawning. Startup failure/configuration-change handling and shutdown guards remain unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the unchanged host-side startup cardinality and joining. Performance differences inside the newly pinned native runtime cannot be established from version numbers or lockfile hashes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK package source/native implementation was unavailable through the repository tools; startup duration and package-size differences are not established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No concrete diff-introduced eager initialization, additional subprocesses, filesystem fan-out or lost startup sharing is visible.

Scenarios.Scenario: Microsoft account discovery, service selection, model availability and conversation create/resume after restart
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Discovery waits for setup-session creation and sequential login steps. Selection confirms the active account before becoming ready. Conversation create/resume waits for authenticateSession and its active-account verification before finalization. Catalog refresh obtains the setup session before fetching the catalog.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the setup session, begin/advance/cancel runtime login, and query the active account.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One begin and flow-dependent sequential advances per login, followed by one verification on successful completion/selection. getActive replaces one get({query:{kind:'activeAccount'}}) call; it does not add account enumeration or multiply calls by service choices.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical call sites and control flow used the former 'loki' account discriminator and one accounts.get active-account query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Login completion and verification gate service readiness and conversation launch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Runtime authentication obtains host-provided Entra credentials and the model-catalog request reaches the selected service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Runtime-owned authentication work per login; one catalog operation per refresh, not one operation per returned model. The integration fixture verifies authenticated /models or /quota requests, but does not expose all native-runtime cache decisions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same token-provider bridge, catalog refresh path and selected-service network access before the API rename.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Authentication gates login; catalog retrieval gates publishing available models.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cancel login and disconnect/delete setup or rejected newly created sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing cleanup for the owned attempt/session, including late cancellation; unchanged by all three production hunks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same ownership, cancellation, disconnect and deletion paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reset/replacement awaits cleanup; failed launch cleans up before propagating.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The supported discovery outcome has two distinct service choices. Each successfully signed-in conversation performs one active-account verification; N newly opened/reopened conversations retain the pre-existing N verifications. One setup session is shared within a runtime lifecycle.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: getSession uses a service-wide Sequencer to serialize setup restoration; later callers reuse the restored setup session. Each conversation's login advances sequentially, while independent conversation logins are not globally limited. No scheduling or limiter changes were added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Ready/choiceRequired discovery avoids repeating discovery. The setup session is reused until release/reset/restart; restoration is shared through getSession. Token-provider cancellation, credential waiting, cleanup and failure behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the production edits are discriminator/API-shape migrations with unchanged loops, call sites, ownership and verification multiplicity. Actual getActive native implementation was not available.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native authentication latency, network caching and simultaneous conversation prevalence are unmeasured; no changed multiplicity is evidenced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression: filtering still scans the same bounded choice list and active-account verification remains one boundary call at the same points.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send ordinary/Fusion chat requests and present incremental model output
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After session preparation and attachment conversion, session.send submits the prompt; visible first output depends on model/network progress and SDK event delivery. Host message-delta callbacks publish incremental ChatResponsePart/ChatDelta actions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit one logical prompt to the SDK session and receive output events; emit incremental chat actions toward the client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One send per submitted prompt, with output actions proportional to delivered chunks. The host emit path already supports both streamed deltas and complete messages; dependency-internal before/after chunk counts are unavailable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same send and event callbacks existed with SDK 2.0.1. PR metadata claims earlier Fusion streaming, but source evidence is insufficient to establish changed event cardinality or additional host cost.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Submission and event delivery gate first visible output; incremental publication does not await complete inference.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Runtime issues model inference through its configured network/proxy path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Runtime-controlled calls per model workflow; neither model-call fan-out nor an increase in concurrent network requests is established by the repository diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Already used the runtime model/network path. The dependency version bump alone does not prove a request-count or concurrency change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Inference response progress gates output and turn completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist an execution eligibility marker before the first SDK execution for the session backing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once before first execution while _sdkExecutionStarted is false, with existing cancellation restoration; not per output chunk.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same first-execution marker and dispatch sequencing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial dispatch awaits marker persistence; later operations skip it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Prompt/attachment bytes, model output chunks, calls within a Fusion workflow and concurrently running chats. Each observed text delta uses its content, not a freshly serialized complete transcript.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: _sdkExecutionSequencer serializes execution-marker changes and dispatch, but explicitly lets issued SDK operations finish concurrently. Fusion complete-message chunks are grouped by phase and call key and removed on completion. Host scheduling is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing response-part IDs are reused for deltas. Fusion chunk grouping releases completed keys; no new host cache or retention policy is added. Runtime/model prompt caching is outside the available dependency implementation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the existing host send/delta path and dispatch concurrency. Insufficient implementation evidence for a dependency-internal streaming regression or provenance-qualified performance fix.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK/runtime sources were unavailable; actual Fusion streaming behavior, chunk frequency, network-call count and timing cannot be independently compared. No benchmark numbers inferred from the PR description.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance issue or regression-fix learning signal. Prompt snapshot grammar rewording does not establish additional model requests, large payload growth or expensive parsing work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve managed policy before session launch and maintain the managed-settings schema baseline
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session configuration awaits managed-settings resolution before opening/finalizing the runtime session. The schema snapshot is consumed only by a dedicated sessionless integration test.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ask the runtime to resolve managed settings for the client and optional credential/working directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One issued query per concurrent unique RPC/credential/directory key, not per model or schema property. Existing integration expectations remain four completed resolutions for four successful launch paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same resolve call, in-flight joining, timeout and launch placement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Policy resolution gates launch configuration, with the existing 30-second timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the complete runtime schema via RPC and JSON.stringify it for the baseline comparison.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One schema retrieval/stringification for this integration test; added schema text is fixed-size, not an input-dependent allocation loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same full-schema retrieval and serialization; the baseline lacked the two new optional list schemas.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only blocks the integration test, not a product startup or rendering path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compare the schema baseline or regenerate it under the explicit update environment flag.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One snapshot read/comparison or write per test invocation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct runtime RPC identities, credentials and working directories for concurrent launch queries; a fixed schema with two additional optional list definitions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: CopilotManagedSettingsResolver joins in-flight requests by RPC object and JSON key [token, workingDirectory]. Distinct keys may run concurrently; no new query loop or limiter change is introduced. Test schema retrieval runs once in its test.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Host shares only in-flight queries and removes them on settlement, including failures. Freshness/fallback caching belongs to the runtime. Invalidation cancels the existing generation and replaces the WeakMap; all unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the changed schema file is test data and host-side resolution multiplicity/coalescing is unchanged. New runtime policy implementation is not inspectable.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime policy-fetch/cache latency and the implementation of the newly supported policy fields are unknown, rather than evidenced new host work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced fan-out, defeated coalescing or scaling serialization mechanism in the changed code.

Scenarios.Scenario: Compact conversation history and reopen it after Agent Host restart
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Explicit compaction awaits runtime history.compact and its summary; reopening awaits runtime/session startup and persisted history reconstruction before displaying restored turns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request compaction; retrieve persisted session events in backward pages of at most 1000.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One explicit compact request; history reads scale by event-log pages per uncached scope, not one request per restored turn. Warm same-scope callers join/reuse reconstruction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same compact RPC and paginated, memoized event reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Compaction waits for its result; restored history waits for required pages and mapping.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reconstruct host turns using session database metadata and restore stored outputs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing reconstruction over retrieved events, including a shared batched stored-output lookup for parent/subagent chats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical reconstruction and database path; only recorded fixture prose changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for cold restored transcript materialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Runtime obtains a compaction summary from the model; the capture records the summary and subsequent context-bearing request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The capture changes response/request text within the same exchange structure; no added exchange or additional request loop is present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same recorded exchanges and live compaction boundary, with earlier wording.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Live compaction awaits summary generation; replay consumes the captured response.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Persisted event count E per requested primary/all scope and summary text size. The changed capture contains one fixed small exchange sequence, with reworded summary and context-preface text.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Compaction dispatch follows the existing execution sequencer; issued operations may finish concurrently. History pagination follows cursor-dependent reads, while same-scope reconstructions share a memoized promise.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: _mappedEventsMemo caches primary/all reconstruction independently and removes rejected promises for retry. Runtime restart resumes persisted data. The fixture changes do not alter invalidation, pagination or cache ownership.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that capture edits do not introduce runtime control-flow or request-count changes. SDK-internal persistence/compaction changes remain unavailable for direct comparison.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Long-history sizes and native compaction durations are not measured. The capture alone cannot establish general performance changes inside the upgraded runtime.
Scenarios.Verdict: No concrete regression from the fixture changes or exposed host history path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass against base 742a9ae378720f2526ed7128fbc47ec2a285f1b1. Inspected all 15 changed-file inventory entries and every diff page (all pagination terminated), production account-flow callers/ownership, runtime startup, managed-policy sharing, streamed output and history reconstruction. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance finding qualifies, and no source/provenance-backed regression fix was established. The required guide was requested but tool output was truncated; learned-regression guidance was loaded. SDK/native runtime implementation was unavailable for inspection, limiting claims about the dependency upgrade.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
